title: Introduction To Respiratory Therapy Pharmacology
description: An in-depth study of drug groups commonly used in the treatment of respiratory diseases. Intended for students in the Respiratory Therapy Program; enrollment is limited to students accepted in the program.
outcomes: Describe the mechanism of bronchospasm and differentiate the pharmacologic effects of sympathomimetic bronchodilators, parasympatholytics, xanthine bronchodilators, mucus-controlling agents, surface-active agents, cold and cough agents, corticosteroids, and mediator antagonists.
Describe the principles of drug action.
objectives: Calculate drug dosages from prepared-strength liquids.
Describe the principles of drug action.
Compare and contrast the autonomic effects in the cardiopulmonary system.
Differentiate the pharmacologic effects of various respiratory medications.
Based upon patient's condition, select the appropriate respiratory pharmacologic agent.
content: Principles related to respiratory therapy drugs, especially nebulized drugs
Autonomic effects in the cardiopulmonary system
Constriction of the smooth bronchial muscles
Pharmacologic effects of various respiratory medications
